description: Explains why fixed-root dynamic programming can miss unrooted topological embeddings, derives the M1/M2 two-branch optimization, and distinguishes these paper arguments from what existing Lean proofs establish.

learning_objectives: Explain why the 2016 fixed-left-root shortcut fails for skipped-path embeddings
Characterize the two selected sides of a highest skipped realized-path vertex
Derive the M1/M2 unrooted decomposition with exactly one central skip penalty
Prove that top-two candidates per right terminal suffice for each cardinality-two child matching
Identify the correct all-root-pairs Lean baseline and the still-open fixed-root structural theorem
